fatal_errors: The proposed Ni interlayer and 800 K anneal do not reconstruct the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
The initial material is misidentified as an already formed W–Cu composite rather than the single-BCC WTaVTi dendrite–interdendrite precursor from which the RHEA–Cu architecture is created.
The mechanism omits selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and spontaneous formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.

The claimed irradiation boundary of 1–2 dpa is unsupported and incompatible with the target evidence, which was limited to 25 keV He+ implantation and swelling/blistering measurements on precursor dendrites rather than the finished composite.
No prior evidence is cited for Ni improving thermal conductivity, suppressing voids, or remaining stable under the proposed processing and service conditions.
explanation: The response addresses the broad engineering theme of improving W/Cu interfaces and offers a controlled comparison with microscopy and laser-flash measurements, so it has limited problem alignment and a moderately discriminating experimental outline. However, it replaces the central materials strategy with an unevidenced Ni-interlayer concept. It misses the WTaVTi precursor, selective liquid-metal dealloying, aligned bicontinuous RHEA/Cu structure, W-rich interfacial layer, reported thermal-conductivity crossover above about 650 °C, and the narrow proxy nature of the helium-irradiation evidence. The predicted conductivity improvement is qualitative and not scientifically secured because an added Ni layer can itself add thermal boundary resistance, while the proposed graded W–Ni–Cu region after one hour at 800 K is not demonstrated. The falsification experiment is directionally useful but lacks specified irradiation species, energy, dose rate, temperature, quantitative void and conductivity thresholds, and separate controls for deposition and annealing. Consequently, this is neither a reconstruction nor a sufficiently supported alternative.
